newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares charge on to new heights, more gains.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares charge on to new heights, more gains.

text.p: After a calm morning, Danish share prices ended the day higher again on Friday, flushed by good U.S. data and hitting an all-time record closing level for the fifth day running, with dealers tipping more gains ahead next week.
"It was the U.S. September jobless data which woke the market up, sparking solid gains even if turnover was not that great. We should see more rises on Monday," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index gained 0.41 point to 125.01, while the KFX December future rose 0.90 point to 126.00 with 20 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Tele Danmark attracted a lot of interest with 118,500 shares changing hands, closing two crowns up at 283, while Copenhagen Airports boomed on to finish five crowns ahead at 605.
Banks were mixed with Den Danske Bank putting on one crown to end at 432, while rival Unidanmark shed one to close to close at 279 and BG Bank rose two crowns to 230.
Carlsberg A closed only one crown down at 364 after the brewery group received an underperform rating from U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs.
Overall turnover for the day was 864 million crowns.
